film.title: Crunch Time on the Farm: The Incredible Cleveland Tenure of Jack Morris
film.description:
August 7th, 1994. Fenway Park. The Cleveland Indians are playing their best baseball in almost forty years, and their starting pitcher has a wheat harvest on his mind.

Jack Morris grew up in St. Paul, Minnesota, a city, not the country. His homecoming came in 1991: ten shutout innings in Game 7 for his hometown Twins. Three years later, Cleveland signed him to a prove-it deal while he flew home to his Montana wheat farm between starts. "It's crunch time on the farm," he told Mike Hargrove. Two days later, Cleveland released him by phone. Three days after that, baseball went on strike.

A JuiceBall film from JuiceboxNation.com, with Hardwood Bricks and 19 North Films. Written and narrated by Matthew Hagan, who was at Game One at Jacobs Field in 1994. Matthew appears in part as an AI avatar made with HeyGen. Nora Lindgren is a fictional AI anchor and is not affiliated with the University of St. Thomas. Music is original.

Sources: AP (Aug. 10, 1994); Seattle Times/Knight-Ridder (Oct. 16, 1994); National Baseball Hall of Fame; SABR BioProject and Games Project; Vince Guerrieri in Defector (Oct. 31, 2022), citing the Cleveland Plain Dealer; MLB.com; Wikipedia.

reels.title: It's crunch time on the farm
reels.text: August 1994. Pennant race. Jack Morris gets pulled at Fenway and tells his manager: it's crunch time on the farm. By the 12th inning he's on a plane to Montana.

reels.title: Whatever one does on a ranch
reels.text: A 5.60 ERA, 8.67 over his last five starts, and a wheat farm 1,500 miles away. Cleveland's GM had the last word.
